## Task: Adversarial review: WK-0183 explore_code mode spec + DEC-0043 registry deferral

### Context
# HO-0064: Adversarial review: WK-0183 explore_code mode spec + DEC-0043 registry deferral

## Read First
- wiki/issues/WK-0183.md
- wiki/decisions/DEC-0043.md
- packages/dispatch-core/src/ho.ts
- packages/dispatch-core/src/schemas.ts
- packages/dispatch-core/src/admission.ts
- packages/dispatch-core/src/assemble.ts
- packages/dispatch-core/src/capture.ts
- packages/dispatch-core/src/recovery-block.ts
- packages/dispatch-mcp/src/tools.ts

## Objective
Adversarially review the WK-0183 spec for adding explore_code as the fifth dispatch mode, plus its ratified acceptance plan. Try to BREAK it before code is written. Priority attack surfaces: (a) touchpoint completeness — the table claims 8 files; hunt for MORE closed vocabularies, enums, switches, or mode lists the spec missed (the ReportedRole union in recovery-block.ts was already found this way; find the next one — check pipeline.ts mode gates, CLI, MCP instructions, tests asserting closed mode sets); (b) spec-vs-code claims — verify every file:line the spec cites still holds; (c) the mode semantics — web forbidden, write_scope forbidden, WK-optional, validation false, verdict mirrors research: does any of these contradict how admission.ts/assemble.ts/capture.ts actually treat non-implement modes; (d) the 4-tier acceptance plan — would passing all 4 tiers still allow a broken or regressed mode to ship (name the concrete hole); (e) the research Zod gap fix — is fixing schemas.ts:9 and tools.ts:41 sufficient, or does the missing-research bug extend further; (f) DEC-0009 discipline — any shape in this spec that is asserted without a capture.

## Constraints
- Read-only spec critique: do not edit any file.
- DEC-0043 (option B, brute-force over registry) is settled — do not relitigate registry-vs-brute-force; critique the spec AS a brute-force addition.
- The naming pair explore_code/explorer is settled — do not relitigate.
- The AgentChassis comparison in the spec's Evidence section is context, not a target.

## Expected Output
Ranked findings list, most-severe first. Each finding: severity (blocker/major/minor); the exact spec claim or file:line it targets; a CONCRETE failure scenario (specific handoff/dispatch state -> wrong admission result, broken prompt, wrong verdict, or silent regression); suggested fix. Explicitly name the single most likely way this spec ships a broken explore_code mode. If a section is sound, one line saying so — no padding.

## Context
kb dispatch v2 has four modes (implement/code_review/redteam/research). WK-0183 adds explore_code (read-only repo exploration; kb-original — upstream AgentChassis has no analog). DEC-0043 ratified brute-force addition over a mode registry; the registry design is preserved in the WK as the path back. The spec was hardened this session: recovery-block.ts ReportedRole vocabulary found missing from the original 7-file touchpoint table; 4-tier AC ratified (unit, live regression via build HO chain, post-merge 3-family live gate, golden fixture from Pi gate capture). This redteam runs BEFORE implementation — findings feed the implement HO's spec.

- wiki/issues/WK-0183.md
- wiki/decisions/DEC-0043.md
- packages/dispatch-core/src/ho.ts

- packages/dispatch-core/src/assemble.ts
- packages/dispatch-core/src/capture.ts
- packages/dispatch-core/src/recovery-block.ts
- packages/dispatch-mcp/src/tools.ts

## Recovery Signal

As the LAST content in your output, emit exactly one fenced JSON block whose info-string is exactly `kb-dispatch-recovery.v1`. Do not emit ordinary ```json fences, extra JSON candidates, or any content after the closing fence.

Your prose review above is the primary deliverable — it is what gets read and acted on. If you can, emit this block as the last content in your output: it gives the orchestrator structured data for automation, an opportunistic shortcut, not a requirement. A missing block, or one that cannot be parsed, does not fail the run.

`reported_role` is `"redteam"`. `reported_subject` is the handoff id you were dispatched as. `reported_outcome` is one of `no_findings` | `passed_no_blocking_or_medium_findings` | `changes_requested`. `no_findings` requires an empty `findings` array and all-zero `finding_counts`. `passed_no_blocking_or_medium_findings` permits only `low`/`info` findings and zero blocking/critical/high/medium counts. Any blocking, critical, high, or medium finding MUST appear in `findings[]`, MUST use `changes_requested`, and blocks a clean outcome.

`findings`, `finding_counts`, and `reviewed_controls` are REQUIRED for this role. Each finding is `{id, title, severity, blocking, affected_paths, control_id}` — `severity` is one of critical|high|medium|low|info, `affected_paths` is an array of `{"path": "src/foo.ts", "line": 42}` (or `"line": null` when no specific line applies). `finding_counts` (`{total, blocking, critical, high, medium, low, info}`) MUST match `findings`. Each `reviewed_controls` entry is `{control_id, result}` with `result` of `pass` or `fail`, listing controls you actually reviewed.

Your chat response outside the block is free narrative for the operator — it is never parsed.

      "id": "F1",

    "total": 1,

      "result": "fail"
    }
  ]
}
